title: Separation of sedimentary phytoliths from other biogenic silica particles for triple oxygen isotope analysis
author: Mention, Aleman, et al.

steps.title: Extract bulk amorphous silica
steps.instruction: Process 1–3 g of dry sediment to extract bulk amorphous silica following the procedures of Crespin et al. and Aleman et al.; during any heating phases keep temperatures ≤ 50 °C for the first phase and ≤ 80 °C for the second phase to avoid dissolution of the silica.

steps.title: Classify and count silica particles
steps.instruction: Under a microscope, classify each amorphous silica particle by biological origin, morphology and size; count particles for each class (minimum count ≥ 10). Compute a 95 % confidence interval (CI) for the proportion p of each class using CI(p)=np ± Z1‑α/2 × √[np(1‑np)/n] with Z1‑α/2 = 1.96. For classes with fewer than 10 particles assign an uncertainty of ± 2.

steps.title: Estimate silica mass proportion
steps.instruction: For each morphological class, calculate particle volume using the geometry appropriate to the class (parallelepiped, cylinder or sphere) as listed in Table 2, then multiply by the class‑specific density (2.1 g cm⁻³ for diatom frustules and sponge spicules, 2.3 g cm⁻³ for phytoliths) to obtain silica mass. Propagate the counting CI to obtain a CI for the mass proportion.

steps.title: Select appropriate mesh size
steps.instruction: Choose a cellular sieve mesh (20 µm or 40 µm) that removes the longest non‑phytolith particles while minimizing phytolith loss; in this study diatom frustules and sponge spicules were typically > 20 µm, so 20 µm or 40 µm sieves were used. Optionally simulate filtration by excluding all particles larger than the chosen mesh and assuming 100 % removal to predict the outcome.

steps.title: Perform filtration with deflocculant
steps.instruction: Process the silica suspension as follows:

substeps.instruction: Add a sodium metaphosphate solution (Na(PO₃)₆) buffered to pH 7 as a deflocculant to disperse particles.
Filter the suspension through the selected cellular sieve mounted on a centrifuge tube; stir manually with a Pasteur pipette while filtering to aid passage of small particles.
Centrifuge the filtrate to collect any remaining particles.
Repeat the filtration with the same mesh until the filtrate appears transparent.

steps.title: Evaluate filtration effectiveness
steps.instruction: Compare the phytolith mass proportion in the final filtrate to the initial phytolith mass proportion CI. Filtration is effective if the filtrate proportion exceeds the upper bound of the initial CI. If the phytolith proportion declines, repeat the procedure with the alternative mesh size to improve removal of non‑phytolith particles while minimizing phytolith loss.
